title: Sort the numbers into the smallest set they belong to
instructions: Each card shows a number. Drag it into the smallest number set that contains it. Tip: every natural number is also whole, integer and rational, but we want the SMALLEST set the number belongs to. Numbers that are not rational go into the 'Irrational' bin.

bins.name: Whole only
bins.description: Whole numbers that are NOT natural — i.e. just zero.

bins.name: Integer only
bins.description: Integers that are not whole numbers — i.e. negative integers.

bins.name: Rational only
bins.description: Rationals (p/q with q ≠ 0) that are not integers, including terminating and recurring decimals.

bins.name: Irrational
bins.description: Numbers that cannot be written as p/q with integer p, q (e.g. √2, π).

items.explanation: 7 is a counting number, so it belongs to N (the smallest set).
0 is whole but not natural — naturals begin at 1.
−4 is an integer, but negatives are excluded from W and N.
Same reasoning as −4: integer, not whole.
3/5 is rational; not an integer because 3/5 has a fractional part.
0.875 = 7/8, a terminating-decimal rational; not an integer.
−2/3 is rational; not an integer because of the fractional part.
√2 cannot be written as p/q with integers p, q — it is irrational.

items.name: π
items.explanation: π is a famous irrational number; its decimal expansion is non-terminating and non-repeating.
Pattern grows; non-terminating and non-repeating, so irrational.
